questions.question: What is the core promise of the American Dream?
options: Success through merit and hard work, regardless of birth
questions.explanation: The Dream promises equal opportunity, upward mobility and success through merit rather than birth.

questions.question: What pattern did the classic immigrant version of the American Dream follow across generations?
options: First generation survival and hard labor; second generation stability; third generation professional careers
questions.explanation: The timeline often ran: survival and sacrifice, then stability and education, then middle-class professional life.

questions.question: Why was the American Dream not equally available to everyone?
options: Black Americans faced legal barriers until the 1960s and Asian immigrants were banned for decades
Everyone always had the same opportunities
Only the rich were allowed to immigrate
The Dream was a government program with quotas
questions.explanation: Legal segregation, the Asian exclusion acts (1882-1943) and other barriers excluded whole groups from the Dream.

questions.question: How did Italian immigrants around 1900 experience America at first?
questions.explanation: About 4 million Italians faced discrimination and worked dangerous jobs in mining, construction and factories.

questions.question: Which symbol is most associated with the immigrant promise of America?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty, welcoming arrivals to New York, symbolises the promise of opportunity for immigrants.
